## Norfolk Southern Corp. (CIK 702165) — Operating Efficiency and Profitability, FY2022–FY2024

**Basis:** Consolidated GAAP annual figures from the FY2024 Form 10-K (filed 2025-02-10, accession 0000702165-25-000008), which reports 2024, 2023 and 2022. "Operating ratio" = railway operating expenses ÷ railway operating revenues (the company's own definition, a measure of revenue consumed by expenses); "operating margin" = income from railway operations ÷ revenue. These are distinct metrics and are reported separately below.

**Reported results (USD, from the database):**

| Metric | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Railway operating revenues | $12,745M | $12,156M | $12,123M |
| Railway operating expenses | $7,936M | $9,305M | $8,052M |
| Income from railway operations | $4,809M | $2,851M | $4,071M |
| Net income | $3,270M | $1,827M | $2,622M |

Fact IDs: revenue 859715 / 859727 / 859736; expenses 847153 / 847165 / 847174; operating income 855238 / 855250 / 855259; net income 854451 / 854469 / 854482.

**Derived ratios (calculated from the above operands):**

| Ratio | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operating ratio | 62.3% | 76.5% | 66.4% |
| Operating margin | 37.7% | 23.5% | 33.6% |
| Net margin | 25.7% | 15.0% | 21.6% |

**Interpretation of the change:**

- **2023: sharp deterioration.** Revenue fell 4.6% while operating expenses rose 17.2%, pushing the operating ratio up 14.2 percentage points to 76.5% and cutting operating margin by 14.3 points to 23.5%. Net income fell 44% and net margin dropped 10.6 points. The 10-K attributes this to the Eastern Ohio (derailment) incident — net expenses of $1.1 billion in 2023 — plus lower revenues and higher non-incident operating expenses from inflation and operational investments (chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:86400).
- **2024: substantial recovery, but not back to 2022.** Revenue was roughly flat (−0.3%), but operating expenses fell 13.5%, lowering the operating ratio by 10.1 points to 66.4% and lifting operating margin 10.1 points to 33.6%. Net income rose 44% and net margin recovered 6.6 points. Management cites operational improvements while handling 5% higher volumes, lower net Eastern Ohio Incident expenses, and $433 million of gains on railway-line sales (chunks :84800 and :86400).

**Important caveat on comparability:** the 2024 improvement is partly non-recurring. On the company's own non-GAAP reconciliation, the *adjusted* operating ratio was 65.8% in 2024 versus 67.4% in 2023 and 62.3% in 2022 — i.e., only a 1.6-point adjusted improvement year over year, and still 3.5 points worse than 2022 (chunk :91200). So on a like-for-like basis, efficiency and profitability recovered modestly in 2024 but remained below the 2022 level; the headline GAAP swing overstates the underlying improvement because 2023 carried the incident charge and 2024 benefited from asset-sale gains.

**Uncertainty:** the database contains only FY2023 and FY2024 annual reports for this company, so 2022 figures are taken from the comparative columns of the FY2024 10-K rather than a standalone FY2022 filing; the values are consistent across the filings present.
